---

Positioning: "OpenTelemetry-native observability with distributed tracing across your
complete AI stack." "a complete solution designed to monitor and optimize your entire AI
stack" / "end-to-end observability across all components."

Monitors:
- LLM performance: response times, throughput, availability across providers; user
  interactions, prompts, completions
- Cost: "real-time spend tracking, cost optimization, and budget management for LLM usage";
  token consumption patterns + efficiency
- Quality & safety: "hallucination detection, factual accuracy verification, and content
  quality scoring"; "toxicity detection, bias assessment, and compliance tracking"
- Agent systems: total invocations, usage distribution by source; agent cost USD + per-agent
  breakdown; p95 operation duration; avg latency by agent and provider
- VectorDB: similarity search response times + throughput; insert/update/delete ops; memory
  usage + storage efficiency
- MCP: session management, connection stability, protocol compliance; tool usage patterns +
  availability
- GPU: utilization, compute efficiency, throughput; temperature + cooling; memory + power

Named tech:
- OpenLIT - open source SDK, "monitor, diagnose, and optimize generative AI systems",
  "supporting 50+ GenAI tools such as LLMs, vector databases, and frameworks such as
  LangChain and CrewAI", OpenTelemetry-native, follows GenAI semantic conventions
- OpenLIT Operator - "zero-code AI observability to Kubernetes by automatically injecting and
  configuring OpenTelemetry instrumentation into your pods"
- OpenTelemetry + GenAI semantic conventions
- Model Context Protocol (MCP)
- Frameworks named: LangChain, CrewAI

Customers: none found on the docs page or blog posts reviewed.
